    A/B test

    A/B testing sends two versions to a small slice of your list, watches which one performs better, then automatically sends the winner to everyone else. The trick: change one thing between A and B — the opening line, the offer, or the call-to-action — so you can tell what actually moved the needle.

    ScriptTag triggerSteps
    Create your first script
    Scripts are talk tracks that pop up on screen during calls based on lead tags. They keep your team on-message and consistent.
    FSBO outreach Call script

    Turn for-sale-by-owners into listing appointments without sounding like every other agent calling them.

    1. Open: “Hi, I’m calling about the home on {{contact.address}} — am I speaking with the owner?”
    2. Probe: How are showings going? What’s the timeline if it doesn’t sell in 30 days?
    3. Value: “I have 3 pre-approved buyers searching this exact area right now.”
    4. Close: Ask for a 15-minute walkthrough — no listing pitch, just a buyer match.
    Pops on tag: FSBO
    Expired listing Call script

    Re-list homes that just fell off the MLS — empathy first, marketing plan second.

    1. Open: “I noticed your listing came off the market — frustrating, right?”
    2. Diagnose: What do you think kept it from selling — price, photos, traffic?
    3. Differentiate: Walk through our 21-day relaunch plan (staging + SMS buyer list).
    4. Close: Book a no-obligation pricing review this week.
    Pops on tag: Expired
    Buyer qualification Call script

    First call with a new buyer lead — qualify budget, financing and timeline in under 5 minutes.

    1. Rapport: Reference the listing they inquired on — “what caught your eye?”
    2. Financing: Pre-approved yet? If not, offer our lender intro.
    3. Criteria: Beds/baths, areas, must-haves vs. nice-to-haves, budget ceiling.
    4. Timeline: “If we found the right home next week, would you be ready?”
    Pops on tag: New buyer
    Missed-call callback Call script

    Return an inbound call we missed — speed-to-lead matters most in the first hour.

    1. Open: “Hi {{contact.first_name}}, sorry we missed you — returning your call about the listing.”
    2. Recap: Confirm which property they called about; pull it up while talking.
    3. Advance: Offer the two next showing windows — “today at 5 or tomorrow at noon?”
    Pops on: Missed call

    Registration

    Why do I have to do this?

    US phone carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon) require every business to register before it’s allowed to send texts — it’s how they block spam. Skip it and your messages get filtered or blocked. ReadySMS files all the paperwork for you — you just confirm a few details, and you can start texting right away while approval finalizes in the background. Below, each business you register is a business profile, and each kind of texting it does (marketing, customer care, etc.) gets its own registration. (Carriers call these a “brand” and a “campaign” — same thing.)

    —Businesses
    —Numbers
    —Daily SMS cap?The most texts you can send per day across all carriers, at your current trust level. It’s an estimate for a normal mix of phone numbers — carriers set the limit from your 10DLC trust score, and it resets at midnight. Brand vetting below raises it.

    Protections
    Guardrails applied automatically to every send
    All protections on
    TCPA litigator scrub
    Checks every contact against known TCPA litigators & serial filers before the first message goes out. Recommended — leave on. Priced per contact (see tiers below).
    DNC complainers
    Blocks people who actively file FCC / Do-Not-Call complaints. Recommended — leave on.
    Federal DNC registry
    Blocks every number on the national Do-Not-Call registry. ⚠ Heavy reach loss — that's most US consumer cell numbers. Off by default; only enable if your program requires full DNC suppression.
    State DNC registries
    Blocks numbers on state Do-Not-Call lists. ⚠ Reduces reach. Off by default.

    Federal & state quiet hours (8:00 AM–9:00 PM in each contact’s local time, tighter in FL & OK) are always enforced — marketing texts never go out overnight. Want a tighter hold? Set your own window below and it’s applied automatically on top of the legal hours. Leave it at 9:00 PM–8:00 AM and only the legal floor applies.
    to
    Active days
    Pick the days texts are allowed to go out. Quiet hours apply within each active day.
    Weekend window
    Use a tighter window on Saturdays & Sundays (carriers scrutinize weekend sends more).

    Auto opt-out handling Always on
    STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE and similar replies are honored instantly and synced back to GoHighLevel as DND. Required by carriers — can’t be turned off.
    Blast defaults
    Applied to every new SMS blast — owners can still change them per-blast
    Require consent confirmation
    Every blast must have the sender confirm lawful consent before it can send. Recommended — keeps your TCPA attestation trail complete.
    Smart Scheduling on by default
    New blasts start with AI per-contact timing enabled. Senders can turn it off for time-sensitive sends.
    Default sending speed
    Cap the rate new blasts send at. “Carrier max” uses the fastest your numbers allow.
    Require approval for large blasts
    Blasts over 1,000 recipients need owner or manager sign-off before sending.
    Opt-out & message footer
    What gets appended to keep every conversation compliant
    How often we re-stamp opt-out & brand info for the same contact. More frequent is safer for carrier compliance; “every 30 days” is the recommended balance.
